exposure: Interpregnancy weight change (>3kg/m2 weight loss, >1kg/m2 weight gain)
cohort: The study included two cohorts of women from an English maternity centre, one (n=14,961) with first and second live-birth pregnancies and another (n=5,108) with second and third live-birth pregnancies, with data collected from 2003 to 2018.
finding: Normal-weight women who lose significant weight (>3kg/m2) between their first and second live pregnancies have greater odds of premature birth compared to normal-weight women who remain weight stable in the interpregnancy period.
